# Results — Study 80 (Cold-Open) on real annual ^GSPC tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  The January Barometer:
does the sign of the S&P 500's January return predict the rest-of-year (Feb-Dec) sign
and magnitude?  ^GSPC daily history from 1950, annual January and Feb-Dec returns
derived from month-end closes (log-returns).  As-of **2026-06-12**.  n = **75 years**
(1951–2025) — tiny effective n, a key caveat throughout.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (annual series) | 1951 – 2025 (75 years) | `704e88442592` |

*Derived from daily closes resampled to month-end; January return = log(Jan-end / Dec-prior-end);
Feb-Dec return = log(Dec-end / Jan-end).  No look-ahead: January signal formed at end of January.*

## Test 1 — Hit-rate vs base rate

The raw hit-rate (sign(Jan) == sign(Feb-Dec)) is **68.0 %** on 75 years.  Against a fair-coin
null (50 %) that is statistically significant (binomial p = 0.0012).  But the market drifts up
most years — the **unconditional Feb-Dec positive rate is 76.0 %** — so the relevant null is
not a coin but *knowing that equity markets trend up*.  Against that base rate the hit-rate of
68 % is *below* it, and the one-sided binomial p-value is **0.957**.  The barometer does not
beat the base rate.

| Test | Hit-rate | p-value | Conclusion |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| vs a coin (50 %) | **68.0 %** | **0.0012** | Significant against a coin |
| vs base rate (76.0 %) | 68.0 % | 0.9570 | **Not significant vs base rate** |

- Up-January hit-rate: **86.7 %** (45 years) — but the base rate for those years is high.
- Down-January hit-rate: **40.0 %** (30 years) — note: down-Jan correctly calls a down rest-of-year only 40 % of the time.
- Permutation p-value (random-label control): **0.0106** — borderline.

## Test 2 — Mean contrast (up-Jan vs down-Jan February-December returns)

| January sign | n | Mean Feb-Dec return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Up January | 45 | **+10.86 %** | — |
| Down January | 30 | **+0.70 %** | — |
| **Contrast (up − dn)** | 75 | **+10.16 %** | **+3.94** |

The contrast is **economically large (10.16 %)** and statistically significant (HAC *t* = 3.94,
Welsh p = 0.0028).  But this reflects a known confound: up-January years tend to be strong bull-
market years — the January return and the rest-of-year return both load on the same underlying
market state (risk-on regimes), not on January having genuine *predictive* content for what comes
next.  The barometer is partly an overlap artefact of regime correlation.

## Sub-period stability — the signal decays post-1985

| Period | n | Hit-rate | Contrast | HAC t | p (coin) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1951–1985 | 35 | 77.1 % | +15.1 % | +4.12 | 0.001 |
| 1986–2025 | 40 | 60.0 % | +5.4 % | +1.99 | 0.134 |

The effect is concentrated in the first half of the sample.  Post-1985, the contrast
(+5.4 %) is below the inference bar (HAC *t* = 1.99) and the hit-rate (60 %) is not
significant versus a coin (p = 0.134).  This is the signature of a fading anomaly —
possibly the well-known effect of publication (Hirsch's almanac became widely read from
the 1970s onward) or post-sample statistical regularisation.

## Barometer strategy vs buy-and-hold

| Arm | Mean/yr | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| Barometer (long if up-Jan, flat if dn-Jan), 10 bp cost | 6.47 % | 0.661 |
| Buy-and-hold Feb-Dec every year | 6.80 % | 0.474 |

The barometer strategy **underperforms buy-and-hold on mean return** (-0.33 %/yr) while
having a higher Sharpe (from avoiding the worst down-Jan years).  But the strategy holds
cash in 30 out of 75 years — in 18 of those years the Feb-Dec return was positive, meaning
the strategy missed real gains.  It is not tradable as a tactical overlay.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.**  The contrast (HAC *t* = 3.94) looks real full-sample but collapses
  post-1985 (t = 1.99), fails the base-rate test (p = 0.957), and is plausibly a regime-
  correlation artefact rather than genuine predictive content.  Effective n = 75 is tiny.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  The strategy underperforms buy-and-hold, sacrifices ~6.8 %
  of the full-year drift (missed positive fbd in 18 down-Jan years out of 30), and the
  signal is not robust enough post-1985 to justify tactical allocation.
- **Beats a coin? — MIXED.**  Beats a fair coin statistically (p = 0.001) but does *not*
  beat the more relevant base rate (p = 0.957) and is not stable across sub-periods.
